content.title: 13.1. Cardiac rehabilitation
content.13.1.1 Comprehensive cardiac rehabilitat: Secondary prevention is most effectively provided through cardiac rehabilitation (CR). All ACS patients should participate in a comprehensive CR programme, which should start as early as possible after the ACS event. CR may be performed in inpatient or outpatient settings, taking age, frailty, prognostic risk stratification, and comorbidities into account. Comprehensive CR is multidisciplinary, supervised by a team usually coordinated by a cardiologist. Core CR components include patient assessment, management and control of cardiovascular risk factors, physical activity counselling, prescription of exercise training, dietary advice, tobacco counselling, patient education, psychosocial management, and vocational support. Several studies show CR after ASCVD events or revascularisation reduces CV hospitalisations, MI, CV mortality and, in some studies, all-cause mortality. Despite benefits, referral, participation and implementation rates are low; many patients relapse to prior habits after CR. There is an unmet need for complementary pathways to centre-based CR and stronger endorsement by physicians and healthcare professionals, and for early partnerships between patients and healthcare teams.
content.13.1.2 Digital health: Telerehabilitation can be an effective strategy to maintain healthy lifestyle and may partially or fully replace conventional centre-based CR. Telerehabilitation covers CR core components including telecoaching, social interaction, telemonitoring, and e-learning. Studies in patients with CAD indicate telerehabilitation can be equivalent to traditional CR for functional improvement, managing risk factors, and increasing patient well-being. Few data exist on effects on recurrent events; a meta-analysis found no significant difference in mortality between telehealth interventions and centre-based supervised CR. Most trials have focused on single CR components (often exercise training/physical activity). More research is needed on outcomes and on health and digital literacy in CR.
